mainTopic: How two ברייתות read the פסוק on kosher locusts (the long-headed locust), and the start of the rules for fish with fins and scales.
overview: The גמרא asks what the תנא דבי רב and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל disagree about, and answers that it is a locust whose head is long. The תנא דבי רב reads ויקרא 11:21-22 as a כלל ופרט, which is narrow, so the long-headed locust is forbidden. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל reads it as a כלל ופרט וכלל, which is wider, so it is permitted. The גמרא objects that the first and last general statements do not match. It answers that this school reads verses this way anyway, and that this verse is the source for that method. Next it asks why למינהו is needed to require all the signs, and answers that סלעם had already widened the group, so we might have widened it without limit. The גמרא explains that the two ברייתות swap the names רשון and ניפול only because each Sage used his local names. Finally it turns to the משנה's rule for fish: a fish that grows its scales later is kosher. The case of a fish that sheds its scales when it leaves the water begins here and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: What do the two ברייתות disagree about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the practical point of disagreement between the תנא דבי רב and the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: On what point do the תנא of the study hall and the תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא has two ברייתות about kosher locusts and asks where they actually differ. This question sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות agree on the basic signs of a kosher locust. The גמרא wants to find the one specific case where they would rule differently.

steps.title: They disagree about a locust with a long head
steps.stepSummary: The point of disagreement is a locust whose head is long.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree about a locust whose head is long.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the disagreement is about a locust with a long head. One תנא forbids it and the other permits it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The named kosher species all have short heads. So the question is whether a locust has to match them in that detail too, or whether having the main signs is enough.

steps.title: The תנא דבי רב reads the verse as a general statement followed by a detail
steps.stepSummary: The תנא דבי רב reads the פסוק as a כלל ופרט. Only species very close to the named ones are permitted, so the long-headed locust is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of the study hall holds: "which have jointed legs" is a כלל. The species ארבה, סלעם, חרגל, חגב together with "after its kind" are a פרט. With a כלל followed by a פרט, the כלל includes only what is in the פרט. Locusts of those species are permitted, and others are not. "After its kind" adds only locusts that resemble them in two ways.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא דבי רב forbids the long-headed locust. He treats "after its kind" as part of the detailed list, so the פסוק ends with details and the rule of כלל ופרט applies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under כלל ופרט, the general phrase is limited to what the list names. "After its kind" adds a little, but only locusts that closely match the named species in two respects. Since all the named species have short heads, a long-headed locust does not match closely enough and is forbidden.

steps.confusionAlert: Here "after its kind" counts as part of the פרט, not as a second כלל. That one reading choice is the whole difference between the two תנאים.

steps.title: The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל reads the verse as general, detail, general
steps.stepSummary: The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל reads "after its kind" as a second כלל, making a כלל ופרט וכלל. That includes anything similar in one respect, so the long-headed locust is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל holds: "which have jointed legs" is a כלל. ארבה, סלעם, חרגל, חגב are a פרט. "After its kind" goes back and makes a כלל again. With a כלל ופרט וכלל, you include only what is like the פרט, and that includes anything resembling it in even one respect.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל permits the long-headed locust. He reads "after its kind" as a new general statement at the end.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלל ופרט וכלל is wider than a plain כלל ופרט: it includes anything similar to the detail. Here even a resemblance in one respect is enough, so a locust with the main signs counts even if its head is long.

keyTerms.meaning: it went back and made a general statement again
general, detail, general; includes whatever is similar to the detail
similar to the detail
in one respect

steps.whatToRemember: The תנא דבי רב reads the פסוק as כלל ופרט, which is narrow (two respects), so the long head is forbidden. The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל reads it as כלל ופרט וכלל, which is wider (one respect), so the long head is permitted.

steps.title: The first and last general statements do not match
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל: the two general statements say different things, so how can they form a כלל ופרט וכלל?
steps.simpleTranslation: But the first general statement is not like the last one! In the first, the תורה says "which have jointed legs": if it has them, eat it; if not, do not eat it. The last general statement, "after its kind," means it is not permitted until it matches in all four signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading of the תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל. The opening כלל and the closing כלל do not mean the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first כלל is broad: having jointed legs alone is enough. The last כלל is narrow: the locust must share all four signs. The question assumes that a כלל ופרט וכלל needs the two general statements to match, so this mismatch seems to break the structure.

the Merciful One, meaning the תורה

steps.kashyaTarget: The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל's reading of the פסוק as כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The first כלל (jointed legs alone is enough) and the last כלל (all four signs are needed) say different things, so they seem unable to form a matching כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: רבי ישמעאל's school does read generals like these as a set
steps.stepSummary: The תנא דבי רבי ישמעאל does build a כלל ופרט וכלל from two general statements even when they are not alike.
steps.simpleTranslation: The תנא of the school of רבי ישמעאל does make deductions from general statements and details like this, even when they are not alike.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 5. It says that the school of רבי ישמעאל really does read the verse this way, even though the two general statements do not match.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 5 the challenge was that two general statements that say different things cannot form a כלל ופרט וכלל. The answer does not deny the difference. It says this school's method allows it anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: General statements and details, a method of reading a פסוק

steps.title: This verse is the source for that method
steps.stepSummary: Wherever we say that רבי ישמעאל's school uses unlike general statements, the source is this case.
steps.simpleTranslation: And what we say in other places, that the school of רבי ישמעאל makes deductions from general statements and details like this, comes from here.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds a side note. The rule from Step 6, which is quoted in other places in ש״ס, comes from this very case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This turns the answer in Step 6 into a known principle. The verse about locusts becomes the source text for this school's method of reading.

steps.title: Quoting the ברייתא: 'למינהו' requires all the signs
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says that 'למינהו' teaches a חגב is kosher only if it has all the kosher signs.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: If it must be called a חגב, I might think it is kosher even without all these signs. So the verse says 'למינהו': it is kosher only if it has all these signs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says that without 'למינהו' we might have thought the name חגב alone is enough. The word 'למינהו' teaches that the kosher signs are also needed.

steps.title: Why would we ever think the signs are not needed?
steps.stepSummary: Since ארבה and חרגול are already named, all kosher locusts must share their signs, so why is a verse needed?
steps.simpleTranslation: Where would the idea come from that it is kosher without all these signs? ארבה and חרגול are written in the verse!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions the ברייתא it just quoted. The idea that a locust could be kosher without the signs seems impossible, so why does the verse need to teach otherwise?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The named species ארבה and חרגול already show us what a kosher locust looks like. Anything included should have to resemble them, so 'למינהו' seems unneeded for this lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Where would this come from?

phrases.english: That it would be kosher without all these signs

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The named species already set the standard, so there was never any reason to think the signs are not needed

steps.title: סלעם widened the category, so we might widen it completely
steps.stepSummary: Because סלעם includes the long-headed locust, we might have included anything, so 'למינהו' is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: If סלעם were not written, it would be as you say. But now that סלעם is written to include the long-headed one, I might say it includes anything at all. So the verse teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9. The word סלעם already brought in something unlike ארבה and חרגול, so we might have thought there are no limits at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: סלעם includes the long-headed locust, even though no named species has a long head. Once one difference is allowed, we might allow every difference. 'למינהו' sets the limit: the signs are still required.

keyTerms.meaning: A named locust species, used here to include the long-headed one

steps.terutzResolutionType: Showing a real reason for the mistaken thought: the wider reach of סלעם made it possible
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since סלעם includes something unlike the named species, perhaps anything called חגב is included

steps.whatToRemember: סלעם widens the category to include the long-headed locust, and 'למינהו' stops it from widening without limit.

steps.title: Why do the two ברייתות swap the names?
steps.stepSummary: One ברייתא says סלעם is רשון and חרגול is ניפול. The other says the reverse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do you say there that סלעם is the רשון and חרגול is the ניפול, but here you say סלעם is the ניפול and חרגול is the רשון?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction between the two ברייתות. They match the names in the פסוק to the everyday names in opposite ways.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'There' is the ברייתא of the תנא דבי רב, and 'here' is the ברייתא of the school of רבי ישמעאל. Each one identifies סלעם and חרגול with the reverse local name.

steps.title: Each Sage used his own local names
steps.stepSummary: Each Sage used the names that were used where he lived, so there is no real argument.
steps.simpleTranslation: This Sage spoke as people did in his place, and that Sage spoke as people did in his place.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction from Step 11. The difference is only in the local names, not in which creatures are being discussed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Different places used the names רשון and ניפול for different species. So the two ברייתות agree about the creatures and only use the names differently.

keyTerms.meaning: Each Sage following the custom of his own place

steps.title: Quoting the משנה's rule for kosher fish
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה: any fish with a סנפיר and קשקשת is kosher.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: And with fish, any fish that has a fin and a scale is kosher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finished with locusts and now quotes the next line of the משנה, about fish. This line sets up the ברייתא that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives two signs a fish needs: a fin and a scale. The next steps will ask what happens when a fish has these signs only at certain times.

A scale, the thin plates covering a fish's skin

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from the discussion of locusts (steps 8-12) to the next topic in the משנה, fish.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fish that has both a fin and a scale is kosher.

steps.title: A fish that grows its scales later is kosher
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that a fish with no scales now, but which will grow them later (like the סולתנית and עפיאן), is מותר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: If a fish has no scales now but will grow them later, such as the סולתנית and the עפיאן fish, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the משנה's rule. It says a fish counts as having scales even if they only grow in later.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה did not say when the fish must have its scales. The ברייתא teaches that it does not need them right now. If this kind of fish grows scales later, it is kosher.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, at the present time
Will grow (them) in the future
Names of two kinds of fish whose scales grow in later
Permitted (here, kosher to eat)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think a fish must have scales at the moment you catch it. Here, a fish that will grow scales later already counts as a kosher fish.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a key idea: a fish is judged by what its kind has over time, not only by how it looks at one moment.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A fish that has no scales now but will grow them later is kosher.

steps.title: A fish that sheds its scales out of the water
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא turns to the opposite case: a fish that has scales now but sheds them when it comes up from the water. Its examples and ruling continue in the next part of the text.

steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא moves to a second case, the reverse of the first one. The text breaks off here, so the examples and the ruling come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 14 the scales came later. Here the scales are there at first and fall off when the fish is pulled from the water. The question is whether scales that do not stay on count.
